tutorial_outline.direct_instruction_goal: Teach the exact classification rule: causal LTI systems are not BIBO stable if any pole has $\Re\{s\}=0$; show this is the boundary case excluded from strict left-half-plane stability.
tutorial_outline.base_case: Use $H(s)=\frac{1}{s^2+4}$ with poles at $s=\pm j2$ to establish the imaginary-axis location and nondecaying oscillatory behavior.
paragraph_plan: Start from prior lesson: pole location determines causal LTI behavior; causality remains the prerequisite condition for all later stability checks.
State the general response form for one pole $s=\sigma+j\omega$ as $e^{st}=e^{\sigma t}e^{j\omega t}$.
Use the $s$-plane rule to define LHP ($\Re\{s\}<0$), RHP ($\Re\{s\}>0$), and imaginary-axis ($\Re\{s\}=0$) categories.
Show why $\Re\{s\}=0$ gives constant-envelope terms, so BIBO response does not decay and stability fails.
Preview the example sequence: zero-real-part identification, origin handling, simple nonzero imaginary poles, and repeated imaginary-axis poles.
